When XHTML is served as application/xhtml+xml every element must carry its namespace prefix, so you write <xhtml:script src="/js/app.js"></xhtml:script> instead of the bare tag. See the XHTML Modularization spec.

To animate the chart inside a compound XHTML+SVG document, bind the SVG namespace and use the prefixed form:
<svg:svg width="400" height="200">
  <svg:script type="application/ecmascript">initChart();</svg:script>
</svg:svg>
Both prefixed and unprefixed forms are equivalent once the namespace is declared.

CVE-2022-1243: urijs before 1.19.11 extracts the protocol incorrectly when the scheme name contains a carriage return, line feed or tab. A crafted value such as java	script:alert(1) is parsed as a relative reference by the library but executed as a scheme by the browser.

Detects a javascript:, vbscript: or data:text/html URI whose SCHEME NAME has been broken up by characters that a URL parser discards but a string-matching sanitizer does not: a raw tab, newline, carriage return or NUL, the numeric character reference for any of them, or a zero-padded numeric reference standing in for the scheme first letter. Also covers the namespace-prefixed svg:script element.

Named character references for whitespace:
		U+0009	CHARACTER TABULATION

	U+000A	LINE FEED
These are only recognised in HTML, not in XML.
